title: Ferrabask and the Cooling Sky-Anvil
story: High on a floating forge-island, Ferrabask the Updraft Bellows fans a cold gale that drains heat from the great sky-anvil, and without that heat the island's anchor-chain cannot be mended. The anvil is at 900 degrees and Ferrabask's gale cools it by 45 degrees every minute. Mr 6 cranks the coal-feeder, which adds heat back at 18 degrees every minute.
question: How many minutes until the anvil cools to the useless temperature of 414 degrees?
solution: With the coal-feeder helping, the anvil really loses 45 - 18 = 27 degrees each minute.
486 / 27 = 18 minutes before the anvil goes cold.
praise: Finding the temperature drop was smart thinking — the missing step was subtracting the coal-feeder's 18 degrees from the gale's 45 to get the real cooling rate.
hint: Two things happen each minute: heat leaves and heat comes back. What is the NET change per minute?
victory: Mr 6 finishes the chain weld with four minutes to spare, and Ferrabask, out of breath from all that blowing, agrees to work the bellows for the smiths instead.
imagePrompt: A numeral-six knight hammering a glowing orange anvil on a floating rocky forge-island, while a swirling grey wind-beast with bellows-like lungs blasts freezing air across the sparks at sunset.
